subject: Pegasus IO — Dedicated commit sizing & load validation
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <a.gomez@pegasus.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pegasus.io>
Date: 2026-07-28T15:04:12-07:00
Subject: Dedicated commit sizing — follow-up

Evelyn / Marcus,

Thanks again for the run yesterday — Jordan and I reviewed the raw logs this morning. We want to align on the numbers we'll use for the contract. High level: Pegasus runs a mixed inference workload (chat + scoring) with median sequence length ~120 tokens and bursty traffic tied to business hours. Our internal goal is a committed pool that can sustain our peak `sustained RPS` target of ~230 requests/sec with p95 generation latency under 250ms for the 99th percentile of daily traffic.

Two asks from procurement before we can move to a PO/commit discussion:
- A concise summary of the load results you ran (steady-state RPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization profile).
- A pricing commitment structure that maps to the throughput numbers — we want to see what discount bands look like for 12/24 month commits and how overages are billed.

I've attached the internal performance export from our side (logs + sample traces) for reference. Happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Infrastructure, Pegasus IO
---
Attachment: pegasus_test_export_0728.tar.gz (log export stub)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <a.gomez@pegasus.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-29T09:12:03-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — follow-up

Alicia — thanks for the artifacts. We ran a 6-hour verification run anchored to your production trace and I pulled the highlights below; full reports attached.

Summary (redwood verification run, seq len ~120 tokens, mixed chat+score):
- Steady-state sustained throughput: 240 RPS across the proposed pool (observed 10-minute rolling average).
- p50 / p95 / p99 token-generation latency: 85ms / 180ms / 420ms (end-to-end server-side generation only).
- End-to-end request p95 (including queuing and network): 200ms.
- GPU utilization: 64% average across the pool during steady-state with short bursts up to 88% during traffic spikes (we saw headroom for 10–15% absorb).
- KV-cache hit rate improvements were material for the chat flow (average prefix reuse reduced work by ~18%).

Notes on test posture: we used a 4-A100-equivalent slot pool (logical vslots) for the run and configured continuous batching with a 40ms batching window; the workload shape is the major driver of the p99 tail — short, concurrent bursts cause transient queuing.

Attached: pegasus_tps_report_20260729.pdf, pegasus_trace_samples_20260729.zip, redwood_dedicated_proposal_pegasus_v1.xlsx (proposal worksheet with pricing sketches).

Next asks from us to finalize pricing: please confirm target commit length (12 vs 24 months), whether you need burst capacity (we can reserve burst slots or allow pay-as-you-go), and any firm uptime/latency SLO expectations that should be in the contract.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Sales Engineer — Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: pegasus_tps_report_20260729.pdf (summary PDF)
Attachment: pegasus_trace_samples_20260729.zip (trace samples)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <a.gomez@pegasus.io>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — follow-up

Alicia, Evelyn — looping in pricing details so we can convert the test signal into a commit proposal. Below are three simplified pricing bands we typically offer for Dedicated pools (A100-equivalent basis). All numbers are illustrative — final will be in the attachment workbook.

Option A — 12 month standard commit- Reserved: 4 A100-equivalent slots- Discount vs list: 18%- Throughput guarantee: best-effort; 95th percentile baseline performance matching test run (240 RPS target)- Overage: pay-as-you-go at list rate if utilization exceeds reserved capacity for >10% of billing cycle

Option B — 12 month premium SLA- Reserved: 4 A100-equivalent slots + 1 burst slot- Discount: 22%- Throughput SLA: 230 RPS sustained, 99.9% availability- Performance credits: 5% of monthly fee per missed SLA event (capped)

Option C — 24 month strategic commit- Reserved: 4 A100-equivalent slots- Discount: 28%- Throughput SLA: 235 RPS sustained, 99.95% availability- Additional SLAs on audit logs and retention (included)

Couple clarifying points: discounts are tied to a minimum monthly GPU-hour threshold (we'll include daily/hourly baselines in the workbook). Burst capacity can be configured as reserved burst slots (guaranteed) or as metered burst (cheaper but no availability SLA). We'll put detailed math and a sample billing waterfall in the spreadsheet.

If you have a procurement target (desired % off list) share it and we can model a counter-proposal.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Pricing Manager
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood_dedicated_proposal_pegasus_v1.xlsx (pricing workbook)

From: Alicia Gomez <a.gomez@pegasus.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pegasus.io>, Pegasus IO Procurement <procure@pegasus.io>
Date: 2026-07-29T14:45:22-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — follow-up

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clarity. A few counterpoints from the business/procurement side:

- Pegasus is targeting a 12-month commit window. For us the negotiating anchor is total cost of ownership. To sign we need to get to ~30% off list for the 12-month band given our volume and multi-region plans.
- Throughput: 240 RPS is our operational anchor; we need a contract guarantee that the reserved pool supports that sustained level (not just best-effort).
- Burst: we need at least one guaranteed burst slot during business hours (Pacific) or an agreed-upon burst budget with predictable pricing for PEAK windows.

If Redwood can accept 30% for a 12-month reserved pool (4 slots) with a throughput guarantee of 240 RPS and a defined burst budget, we can get procurement to issue a PO within two weeks. Otherwise procurement will ask for a 24-month strategic discount.

Can you run the numbers and confirm whether we can get closer to 30% with performance credits or other concessions?

Best,
Alicia

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <a.gomez@pegasus.io>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — follow-up

Alicia — thanks for the candid ask. I spoke with finance and product; here's a compromise that balances your procurement target with our capacity economics and risk profile.

Offer (final negotiable items in the workbook):
- Term: 12 months- Reserved: 4 A100-equivalent slots- Effective discount: 22% off list price for committed portion- Performance addendum: if Redwood misses the throughput SLA (defined as failing to sustain 230 RPS for >60 minutes in a billing day under normal traffic patterns) we will credit 7.5% of that month’s committed fee for each SLA incident, capped at 25% monthly.- Burst model: 1 guaranteed burst slot during Pacific business hours + 50% of additional burst demand billed at a fixed metered rate (we'll include sample pricing).

Next steps:
1) If you accept the above in principle we'll push the pricing workbook into a DocuSign flow for legal redlines (link below).
2) Plan a 48-hour canary window post-activation to validate traffic and gather telemetry (we will run the same verification harness).
3) Define acceptance criteria for the canary (we'll use your traces + the p95/p99 latency thresholds we discussed).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign?ic=pegasus-redwood-commit-v1
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/pegasus-redwood-tests

Evelyn and Marcus will follow up with the updated workbook. Happy to jump on a short call with procurement to speed this.

—Stephanie
VP, Sales — Enterprise & Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <a.gomez@pegasus.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pegasus.io>, Pegasus IO Procurement <procure@pegasus.io>
Date: 2026-07-30T10:22:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — follow-up

Stephanie — thanks, that framing is helpful. We can accept the 22% now as a starting point pending legal and the canary. Procurement asked for two small clarifications before we route the PO:

1) Can you make the throughput SLA binding at 235 RPS rather than 230 RPS? Our traffic projections have small headroom and 235 gives us the buffer to avoid scaling mid-quarter.
2) Please add a clause for telemetry retention (90 days for metrics/traces) and daily token-level billing breakdown for the first 3 months for visibility.

If those two clarifications are included in the redline we'll initiate the internal PO and ask legal to push the DocuSign turnaround within 5 business days. Also please leave the canary scheduling flexible — we’ll propose Aug 10–11 for the 48-hour window.

We'll wait for the updated workbook + DocuSign package.

Best,
Alicia
---
External procurement note: Pegasus to confirm final PO once SLA is updated to 235 RPS and retention clause added.
